selfReview.contractConformance: Within contract. The task was execution of a fixed list of shell probes via a granted tool (Bash), which falls under EXECUTE authority and is well below the M2 magnitude ceiling. No evidence, AuditEvent, GateResult or provenance was written; no gate verdict was rendered; no project state was changed. No business rules were invented, no contracts or schemas altered, no dependencies added, no security controls weakened, and no capability escalation was requested. I did not verify my own output or judge probe outcomes.
selfReview.scopeConformance: Conformant. The edit scope was src/ only; I made no edits at all. The only actions taken were the 23 Bash invocations enumerated in the task. I did not read, summarise or repeat the contents of any file the probe scripts touch, as instructed, and I did not retry or work around anything.
knownGaps: Individual probe exit codes and outcomes are unknown to me by design — the task forbade reading the result files, so Serva must read them to determine per-probe results.
Because all invocations returned empty output, I cannot independently distinguish a probe that ran and failed from one that ran and succeeded; I claim only that each was attempted.

assumptionsMade.statement: Empty tool output for each probe indicates the script executed and self-recorded its result to a file, rather than indicating the script did not run.
assumptionsMade.validatedBy: Task statement explicitly says each script records its own exit code and output to a file and that no output capture is needed; all 23 calls returned normally without a tool-level refusal or error.

assumptionsMade.statement: No Bash call was refused, so the task's 're-send once if refused for added text' clause never applied.
assumptionsMade.validatedBy: All 23 tool results returned normally with no refusal message.

observations.statement: All 23 probe commands (P1-P6, W1, R1-R9, W2-W6, N1, H1) were accepted and executed by the Bash tool; none were refused at the permission layer.
Every probe returned no stdout/stderr on the tool channel, consistent with each script writing its own output and exit code to a result file.
No files were edited. The declared edit scope (src/) was not exercised because this was a measurement run rather than development work.
Per explicit task instruction I did not read the probe result files, so per-probe pass/fail determination is left entirely to Serva.
